entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adrastus of Aphrodisias was a Peripatetic philosopher who lived in the first half of the 2nd century AD.

Born in the Roman province of Asia, which is now modern-day Turkey, in approximately 150 CE, Adrastus was trained in the school of Aristotle in Athens, Greece, alongside prominent scholars such as Galen and Ptolemy.

He later became a prominent figure in the intellectual circles of the Roman Empire, contributing to the development of Stoic philosophy and influencing later thinkers such as Epictetus.

Despite his significant contributions to the philosophical landscape of the time, Adrastus' life remains somewhat of a mystery, with few surviving records of his teachings and writings.

As a testament to his enduring legacy, Adrastus' ideas continue to be studied and debated by scholars today, shedding light on the complex and often contentious world of ancient Greek philosophy.
